headline: High Alpine Seasonal Access Check
reservation: The highway itself does not require a permit, but camping in the Absaroka-Beartooth Wilderness often requires specific backcountry protocols. Entrance into Yellowstone at the Northeast gate requires a separate National Park pass or fee.

days.title: The Ascent from Red Lodge

stops.name: Rock Creek Vista Point
stops.detail: Walk the paved path for a view of the switchbacks climbing the Hellroaring Plateau.

stops.name: Gardner Lake Pullout
stops.detail: View the high alpine cirque and watch for marmots in the rocky tundra.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for the 68-mile drive; speed is limited by steep grades and sharp turns.
days.note: Check Montana Department of Transportation for daily opening status as snow can fall year-round.

days.title: Top of the World Exploration

stops.name: Beartooth Butte
stops.detail: Photograph the iconic 10,000-foot sedimentary landmark reflected in the alpine lakes.

stops.name: Island Lake
stops.detail: Stop at this high-plateau lake for a short walk along the water’s edge at 9,500 feet.

days.driving: Driving time is negligible between plateau stops, but high altitude may slow walking pace.
days.note: Lightning is a hazard on the exposed tundra during afternoon summer storms.

days.title: Silver Gate and Cooke City
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Top of the World

stops.name: Clay Butte Lookout
stops.detail: A former fire lookout providing 360-degree views of the Absaroka Range and Yellowstone's northern boundary.

stops.name: Cooke City Historic District
stops.detail: Explore the mining history and local general stores of this remote gateway town.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the descent into Cooke City; use low gears to manage brake heat.
days.note: Services in Cooke City are highly seasonal and may close by mid-October.

intel.title: Summit Overlook Limits
intel.text: Small pullouts at the Beartooth Pass summit fill quickly mid-day. Use designated areas only; stopping in the travel lane is strictly prohibited.

intel.title: Tundra Dead Zones
intel.text: Cell service is unavailable for most of the stretch between Red Lodge and Cooke City. Physical maps are recommended for navigating forest service access roads.

intel.title: Gap Planning
intel.text: There are no gas stations on the 68-mile highway section. Refill in Red Lodge or Cooke City before starting the ascent.

intel.title: Annual Road Opening
intel.text: The road typically opens Memorial Day weekend and closes in October. Dates are subject to snowpack levels and official DOT clearing operations.

intel.title: RV Length Restrictions
intel.text: While not prohibited, long vehicles may struggle with tight switchbacks near Red Lodge. Check actual vehicle length against posted advisory signs.

plan.arrival: Fly into Billings (BIL), rent a vehicle, and drive 60 miles to Red Lodge for a morning start on the highway.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are not required for the highway, but powerful engines help with the 10,947-foot climb; check rental brakes before departure.
plan.goldenHour: Rock Creek Vista Point at sunrise offers light hitting the Beartooth Face, though early morning frost can affect road traction.
